sections.what_happened: White House: 'The United States will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections.' Israeli source: 'Hunting season is open as soon as the elections end and it's obvious that they're not going to wait long.' Trump (airfield, Wed night): US not negotiating with Iran; 'something is going to happen very soon, one way or another'; 'Most people think it will happen after the elections.' White House declined to confirm the NYT report ('does not comment on sensitive military plans that may or may not exist'); Pentagon declined to comment.
sections.what_verified: Kelly on-record denial via ABC News; Trump 'very soon' quotes via NewsNation; Straits Times/NYT-carried version of post-midterm plan details (Hegseth-Netanyahu meeting, Iraq flyovers, energy/nuclear/missile targets).
sections.what_disputed: Netanyahu on Thursday denied the NYT reports ('incorrect'), declined to elaborate; some officials say refineries may be spared to limit gasoline prices; Trump has repeatedly vetoed return to major combat ops in 2026 -- decision not made.
sections.why_matters: The White House just put a date on the war: nothing before Nov 3, everything after -- the election is now the fuse. Frame from the Iranian-side bracing (AJ: 'Iran is bracing') + the oil-price constraint.
sections.context: Background: NEW -- White House: no Iran strikes before the Nov 3 midterms; Israeli source: 'hunting season' opens after elections

totw_analysis: Our read: The White House just put a date on the war: nothing before Nov 3, everything after -- the election is now the fuse. Frame from the Iranian-side bracing (AJ: 'Iran is bracing') + the oil-price constraint. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Strike right after Nov 3 ('finish the job') vs retaliation fear -- comments split between pro-strike urgency and anti-strike warnings of Iranian retaliation.
